papers.title: Holographic dark energy through Kruglov entropy
papers.abstract: We study a holographic dark energy model built on the new entropy proposed by Kruglov, $S_K=S_{BH}/(1+\gamma S_{BH}^2)$, with the Granda--Oliveros infrared cutoff $L^{-2}=\alpha H^2+\beta\dot H$ in a flat universe. The Kruglov entropy is smaller than the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy and has a maximum value. We obtain the energy density of the model, the differential equation for the dark energy density parameter, and the expressions for the equation of state parameter, the deceleration parameter and the squared sound speed. At early times the model behaves like the usual Granda--Oliveros holographic dark energy, and the dark energy follows the background with a constant fraction. At late times the Kruglov correction gives a stable de Sitter future when $\alpha>1$, with the final Hubble rate fixed by the entropy parameter. The model gives a matter era followed by a dark energy era, with a transition from deceleration to acceleration near $z\approx0.66$. For larger values of the entropy parameter the equation of state can cross the phantom divide; for the parameters allowed by the data this happens only in the future, if at all. We constrain the model with 31 cosmic chronometer points, Pantheon+ supernovae and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation data, together with a big bang nucleosynthesis condition, using a Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis. We find $H_0=68.0\pm1.6$ km\,s$^{-1}$\,Mpc$^{-1}$, $\alpha=1.19^{+0.10}_{-0.08}$, $\beta=0.61^{+0.06}_{-0.05}$ and the 95\% upper limit $\tilde b=b/H_0^4<0.24$ on the dimensionless Kruglov parameter (for a matter-era dark energy fraction below 0.3), which gives $\gamma<4.9\times10^{-246}$. The present equation of state is $w_{D0}=-0.83\pm0.03$. The model fits the data slightly better than $\Lambda$CDM ($\Delta\chi^2=-4.5$) and is equally good by the Akaike criterion, while the Bayesian criterion and the Bayesian evidence prefer $\Lambda$CDM.

papers.title: A Unified Perspective on Poincar\'e and Galilei Relativity: II. General Relativity: A. Kinematics
papers.abstract: Building on the first paper in this series (Paper~I), a unified perspective on Poincar\'e and Galilei physics in a 5-dimensional spacetime setting is further pursued by consideration of the kinematics of general relativity, with the gravitational dynamics to be addressed separately. The metric of the 5-dimensional affine spacetimes governed by the Bargmann groups considered in Paper~I (central extensions of the Poincar\'e and Galilei groups) is generalized to curved spacetime by extending the usual 1+3 (traditionally `3+1') formalism of general relativity on 4-dimensional spacetime to a 1+3+1 formalism, whose spacetime kinematics is shown to be consistent with that of the usual 1+3 formalism. Spacetime tensor laws governing the motion of an elementary classical material particle and the dynamics of a simple fluid are presented, along with their 1+3+1 decompositions; these reference the foliation of spacetime in a manner that partially reverts the Einstein perspective (accelerated fiducial observers, and geodesic material particles and fluid elements) to a Newton-like perspective (geodesic fiducial observers, and accelerated material particles and fluid elements subject to a gravitational force). These spacetime laws of motion for particles and fluids also suggest that a strong-field Galilei general relativity would involve a limit in which not only $c \rightarrow \infty$, but also $G \rightarrow \infty$, such that $G / c^2$ remains constant.

papers.title: Finite-amplitude establishment beyond local invasion in cooperative chemical networks
papers.abstract: Local kinetic exponents and next-generation radii diagnose infinitesimal invasion, but they need not determine whether a nonlinear organized state is accessible. Motivated by the kinetic component of Gate~7 in a twelve-gate nonequilibrium framework, we study cooperative networks whose productive linearization contains no closed cycle. We prove that an acyclic productive Jacobian has $R=0$ and $\lambda_{\rm kin}=-\min_i d_i<0$ for every drive, while a nonlinear return path can create a stable finite-amplitude branch through a saddle-node. In a canonical catalyst--assembly model, the saddle's stable manifold---not a threshold in either concentration---is the deterministic establishment boundary, so equal-abundance seeds of different composition can have opposite outcomes. At finite copy number, establishment becomes a committor and first-passage problem. For a benchmark protocol with $\Gamma=2$, $\Omega=16$, $\eta=0.02$, and horizon $T=1000$, density-Hill and pair-count generators give first-entrance probabilities $0.633$ and $0.339$; their interpolated half-success drives are $1.900$ and $2.148$, an approximately $13.1\%$ shift. The associated constant-source deterministic system retains a stable low state, so these transitions are fluctuation- and discrete-arrival-enabled. The finite-amplitude regime is not confined to exact acyclicity: a weak linear return leaves a finite interval with $0<R<1$, $\lambda_{\rm kin}<0$, and bistability. A general cooperative-return criterion separates the superlinear local condition from the global return-profile structure required for a fold. The resulting hierarchy of branch existence, basin accessibility, and finite-time stochastic establishment replaces a single onset threshold by a protocol-dependent kinetic criterion.
